好問題！這是關鍵誤解。

## `x86_64-apple-darwin18` **不是一台 Mac**

它是你 Linux 樹上的**一個資料夾標籤**，意思是:

> 「這裡面的東西，是**在 Linux 上做出來的**，但**要拿去 Mac 上跑**。」

完整路徑就是在講這件事:

```
legacyPackages . x86_64-linux . x86_64-apple-darwin18 . hello
                 └─ 在哪做 ─┘   └──── 給誰跑 ────┘
```

你的 PC 沒有變成 Mac。你的 PC 只是**多了一個「做 Mac 程式」的產品線**。

## 工廠比喻

```
你的 Linux PC = 一間台灣工廠
```

工廠裡有幾條生產線:

| 生產線 | 做出來的東西 | 誰能用 |
|---|---|---|
| `x86_64-linux-gnu` | Linux 執行檔 | 你自己 |
| `x86_64-apple-darwin18` | Mac 執行檔 | 拿去 Mac 上跑 |
| `nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d` | RISC-V 執行檔 | 燒到 Andes 晶片 |

工廠一直在台灣。「日本線」不是日本的工廠，是**工廠裡專門做日本規格產品的那條線**。

## 程式碼證明

`pkgs/x86_64-apple-darwin18.nix:5-7`:

```nix
build = x86_64-linux-gnu;        # 做工的: 你的 Linux
host  = x86_64-apple-darwin18;   # 用結果的: Mac
```

再看裡面每一個 derivation 的最後一行 (`pkgs/x86_64-apple-darwin18.nix:56`):

```nix
system = x86_64-linux-gnu.system;   # = "x86_64-linux"
```

**它自己承認: 我在 Linux 上做工。** 沒有任何一行需要真的 Mac。

## 那怎麼可能編出 Mac 程式? 需要兩樣東西

**1. 一個「跑在 Linux、吐出 Mac 程式」的編譯器**

它住在 `x86_64-linux-gnu` 裡面 (不是在 Mac 那個資料夾裡):

```console
(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#x86_64-apple-darwin18-clang      # 這是 Linux 執行檔!
(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#x86_64-apple-darwin18-toolchain
```

**2. Mac 的 header 檔和 library**

就是 `macos-sdk` — 從 Apple 開源的 SDK 解出來的一堆 `.h` 和 stub library。編譯只需要「檔案」，不需要「機器」。

```nix
macos-sdk = lib.bwrapDerivation {
  root = [ x86_64-linux-gnu.stdenv-nocc ];   # 在 Linux sandbox 裡解壓
  system = x86_64-linux-gnu.system;
};
```

有這兩樣，Linux 就能吐出 Mac 的 binary。這叫 **cross compile**。

## 對照: 真正的 Mac 在哪裡?

BSV 也有真正在 Mac 上做工的部分 — `pkgs/aarch64-darwin.nix`，只有 7 行:

```nix
{
  system = "aarch64-darwin";        # ← 這個 job 必須在真的 Mac 上跑
  aarch64-apple-darwin23 = import ./aarch64-apple-darwin23.nix;
}
```

它在 `legacyPackages` 的**第一層**，不在 `x86_64-linux` 底下。

看層級就分辨得出來:

| 路徑 | 做工的機器 |
|---|---|
| `legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.`**`x86_64-apple-darwin18`** | 你的 Linux (cross compile) |
| `legacyPackages.`**`aarch64-darwin`** | 真的一台 Mac |

## 一句話

```
第 2 段 = 誰做工 (system)
第 3 段 = 給誰跑 (host)
```

`legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.x86_64-apple-darwin18` 唸出來就是:
**「在 x86_64-linux 上做，給 x86_64-apple-darwin18 跑」** — 一台機器，兩個名字。

content.text:
好，那兩個字其實比 `build`/`host` 簡單。分開講。

---

# `system` — 給 Nix 看的標籤

`system` **不是第三台機器**。它是 `build` 裡面的**一個欄位**。

為什麼要單獨存在？因為 **Nix 不認識 BSV**。

`build` 和 `host` 是 BSV 自己發明的東西 (就是那個 1142 行的 attribute set)。Nix 完全看不懂。Nix 只認得一個字串:

```nix
system = "x86_64-linux";   # Nix: 好, 這個 job 我丟給 x86 Linux 機器做
```

所以:

```
system  =  build 裡面, Nix 唯一看得懂的那一小塊
```

你在寫 package 的時候，它永遠是同一行，你不用思考:

```nix
system = build.system;
```

`build` = 給**你的 package 檔案**用的 (拿工具、拿 flag)
`system` = 給**Nix**用的 (排工作)

同一件事，兩個讀者。

---

# `target` — 只有「會產生程式碼的程式」才有

普通程式 (hello, verilator, bc) 只有 2 個角色就夠了。
但 **compiler** 需要 3 個，因為它自己會吐出別的機器的程式碼。

以 GCC 為例:

| 角色 | 問題 | GCC 的答案 |
|---|---|---|
| `build` | 誰**編譯 gcc** 這個程式? | 你的 Linux |
| `host` | **gcc 執行檔**跑在哪? | 你的 Linux |
| `target` | gcc **吐出來的程式碼**給誰跑? | RISC-V 晶片 |

`hello` 沒有 `target`，因為 hello 不會產生程式碼。它只會印字。

真實例子 — `pkgs/andes/toolchain.nix:8-13`:

```nix
{
  bsv,
  build,
  host ? build,
  target,          # ← 第三個角色
}:
```

它被這樣呼叫 (`pkgs/linux-gnu.nix:773-782`):

```nix
andes = builtins.mapAttrs (_: config:
  import ./andes/toolchain.nix {
    inherit bsv build;                                        # build = host = 你的 Linux
    target = bsv.legacyPackages.${build.system}.${config.name};  # target = RISC-V
  }) (import ./andes/toolchain-configs.nix);
```

---

# 最重要的一點: 這些是**角色**，不是**東西**

同一個 platform set，在不同地方扮演不同角色。看 `nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d` 這一個東西:

```console
# 這裡它是 target — 我要一個「能產生 RISC-V 程式碼」的編譯器
(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#andes.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
   build=Linux   host=Linux   target=RISC-V
   → 產出: 一個 Linux 執行檔 (riscv64-elf-gcc)

# 這裡它是 host — 我要一個「跑在 RISC-V 上」的函式庫
(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d.libnn
   build=Linux   host=RISC-V
   → 產出: 一個 RISC-V 的 .a 檔
```

**完全一樣的 `nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d`**，一次當 target，一次當 host。

所以「這是什麼平台」問錯了。要問「**它在這個 package 裡扮演什麼角色**」。

---

# 總表

| 字 | 是什麼 | 誰在讀 | 什麼時候出現 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build` | platform set | 你的 package 檔案 | **每一個** package |
| `host` | platform set | 你的 package 檔案 | **每一個** package (預設 = build) |
| `system` | 字串 (在 build 裡面) | Nix | 每一個 package，永遠寫 `build.system` |
| `target` | platform set | 你的 package 檔案 | **只有** compiler / debugger / binutils |

你要加自己的 package，只需要 `build` 和 `host`。`system` 照抄一行，`target` 不用理。

(bsv) $ bsv build /bsv#x86_64-w64-mingw32.andes.vsim  # Windows 版
```

註冊在兩個地方: `pkgs/linux-gnu.nix:902` (native) 和 `pkgs/x86_64-w64-mingw32.nix:315` (cross to Windows)。

## 這個 package 剛好把你學過的東西全用上

**1. source 從內部 git 來** — 不是寫在 package 檔案裡，而是集中在 `pkgs/andes/repositories.nix:292`:

```nix
vsim = lib.fetchGit {
  url = "https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/vsim";
  ref = "main";
  rev = "08ba3645aa2af65dc4747eded41fcfede4df489e";
  submodules = true;
};
```

Andes 自己的 repo 都放在那個檔案，這樣版本集中管理。

**2. 它用 `verilator`** — 就是我們前面看的那個 package:

```nix
root = [ … build.verilator … ];
configureFlags = [ "-DVSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE=${build.prefix}/bin/verilator" … ];
```

注意是 `build.verilator` — verilator 是**做工用的工具**，跑在你的 Linux 上，所以來自 `build`。

**3. 它用 `cmakeBuilder`** 而不是 `configureMake` (加 `-GNinja`)。

**4. 它明確處理 cross compile** — 這是最值得看的部分:

```nix
root = [ … ]
++ (if build.name != host.name then [ build."${host.name}-clang" ] else [ ]);
```

```nix
configureFlags = [ … ]
++ (if build.name != host.name then
      [ "-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=${build."${host.name}-cmake-toolchain-file-clang"}" ]
    else [ ]);
```

翻譯: 「如果 build ≠ host (要做 Windows 版)，就多拿一個 cross clang，並且告訴 cmake 用那個 toolchain file。」

那個 `x86_64-w64-mingw32-cmake-toolchain-file-clang` 你已經見過了 — 在 `pkgs/x86_64-linux/x86_64-linux-gnu.nix` 裡面 (有 `-femulated-tls` 那個註解的)。

| 來自 | 東西 | 為什麼 |
|---|---|---|
| `build` | cmake, ninja, verilator, python, tcl, llvm | 這些是**做工的工具**, 跑在 Linux |
| `host` | `boost`, `zlib` | 這些是**要連進 vsim 的函式庫**, 必須是 host 版本 |

看 `root` 裡面 `host.boost` 和 `host.zlib` 那兩行 — 只有這兩個是 `host.`，其他全是 `build.`。這就是規則「工具來自 build，函式庫來自 host」。

| `x86_64-w64-mingw32` (Windows) | ✓ |
| Mac (darwin18 / darwin20) | ✗ (null) |
| `aarch64-linux-gnu` | ✓ |

```

# AndeSim

AndeSim gives a cycle count for code that you write yourself.

Put two markers in your C function, around the part that you want to
measure. AndeSim runs the program in QEMU at full speed, then measures
the marked region on a cycle-accurate model of an Andes RISC-V core.
The result is one number: the cycles between the two markers.

## Prerequisites

Get these four things before you start.

### A docker image
**A container runtime.** A run always happens inside the AndeSim image.
Use podman to build and run the image.

### Andes RISC-V Toolchain
**An Andes RISC-V bare-metal toolchain (rv64).** The toolchain directory
must contain `bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc`. 
toolchain. Your toolchain compiles your program, and the image build
uses it too. The build mounts the toolchain read-only, and never copies
it into the image.

### Disk space and time.
The image is about 1.8 GB. The build compiles
QEMU, and it makes a simulator from the RTL of the core, so it takes
for a while. You do this one time.

## 1. Build the image

```sh
git clone https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git andesim
cd andesim
scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain /path/to/riscv-toolchain
```

The build makes an image with the name `andesim:v0.1.0`.

All the other steps below start in this `andesim` directory.

## 2. Build the runtime library

```sh
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/riscv-toolchain
scripts/build_runtime.sh
```

This step takes seconds. It makes `build/runtime/`, which holds the C
runtime that your program links against, and the marker header
`andesim/ROI.h`.

## 3. Write a function to measure

Put this in `kernel.c`:

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#define N 256
static int a[N], b[N];

/* noinline keeps the loop inside the measured region: the markers hold
   memory accesses in place, but not work that stays in registers. */
__attribute__((noinline)) static long dot(const int *x, const int *y, int n)
{
        long s = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
                s += (long)x[i] * y[i];
        return s;
}

int main(void)
{
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = N - i; }

        andesim_ROI_begin();
        long s = dot(a, b, N);
        andesim_ROI_end();

# AndeSim image -- one build produces everything a run needs.
#
# Build it with scripts/build_image.sh, which is the supported interface:
#
#   scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <riscv-toolchain-root>
#
# What this build does, and why it is shaped this way:
#
#   * Each source is pinned by commit, not just by ref. A clone layer's cache
#     key is its instruction text, so a branch name alone never changes: a
#     build against a branch that had moved would silently reuse the old clone
#     and ship stale sources. scripts/build_image.sh resolves each ref on the
#     host and passes the commit, and each clone asserts it landed on it.
#   * It clones and builds all three sources itself -- AndeSim, QEMU and the
#     cycle-accurate engine. Users prepare none of them; that setup burden is
#     what the image removes. The build context is empty, so nothing from the
#     building machine can enter the image: no stale build/ directory, no local
#     config.env, no uncommitted edit. The image is reproducible from the three
#     refs alone, and a local change must be pushed before an image carries it.
#   * It builds exactly ONE engine, named by ENGINE. Verilating the RTL is by
#     far the slowest step, and v0.1.0's image supports only this engine.
#   * The engine's RTL comes from the private Andes RD-SW repositories, so the
#     clone steps need a credential. It arrives as a build SECRET, reaching
#     only the RUN steps that clone -- never a layer, never build history.
#   * The RISC-V toolchain is NOT copied in. It is bind-mounted read-only at
#     /opt/riscv-toolchain (scripts/build_image.sh passes --volume), both here
#     and at run time, so the image carries no host path.

ARG VERILATOR_IMAGE=docker.io/verilator/verilator:v5.046
ARG BASE_IMAGE=docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04

FROM ${VERILATOR_IMAGE} AS verilator

# --- env: one build environment for QEMU, the engine, and AndeSim itself -----
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE} AS env

ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends \
      autoconf autoconf-archive automake autotools-dev bison bzip2 \
      ca-certificates clang cmake curl flex g++ git help2man \
      libboost-date-time-dev libboost-dev \
      libboost-filesystem-dev libboost-system-dev libfl-dev libfl2 \
      libglib2.0-dev libpixman-1-dev libreadline-dev libtool lld m4 make \
      ninja-build patch perl perl-doc pkg-config python3-dev python3-pybind11 \
      python3-venv python3-yaml ccache tclsh xz-utils zlib1g zlib1g-dev \
    && apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY --from=verilator /usr/local/share/verilator /usr/local/share/verilator
COPY --from=verilator /usr/local/bin /usr/local/bin

# Reading the private repositories needs git's credential store, and that
# helper WRITES back to its file on success -- so it cannot point at the
# read-only secret mount. Each clone step takes a writable copy and deletes it
# in the same layer, so no credential is ever committed to the image. The
# wiring is per-step rather than a stage ENV, so it does not survive into the
# image a user receives.
ENV GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0

# --- qemu: the functional leg, built here so the user never builds it --------
FROM env AS qemu-build

ARG QEMU_REPO
ARG QEMU_REF
ARG QEMU_REV
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    install -m600 /run/secrets/gitcreds /tmp/gitcreds \
 && GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
    GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
    GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/tmp/gitcreds" \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "${QEMU_REF}" "${QEMU_REPO}" /src/qemu \
 && test "$(git -C /src/qemu rev-parse HEAD)" = "${QEMU_REV}"; \
    rc=$?; rm -f /tmp/gitcreds; exit $rc

# AndeSim is 64-bit-only, so riscv64-softmmu is the whole target list.
# --enable-plugins is what the hybrid handoff plugin needs.
RUN cd /src/qemu \
 && ./configure --prefix=/opt/qemu --target-list=riscv64-softmmu \
      --enable-plugins --disable-werror --disable-libnfs \
 && make -j"$(nproc)" \
 && make install \
 && rm -rf /src/qemu

# --- engine: the cycle-accurate leg, exactly one config ----------------------
FROM env AS engine-build

ARG VSIM_REPO
ARG VSIM_REF
ARG VSIM_REV
ARG ENGINE

# Only the submodules this engine needs: the shared libraries, plus the one RTL
# package its config names. Cloning every RTL package would multiply the build
# for engines this image does not ship.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    install -m600 /run/secrets/gitcreds /tmp/gitcreds \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/tmp/gitcreds" \
 && git clone --depth 1 --branch "${VSIM_REF}" "${VSIM_REPO}" /src/vsim \
 && test "$(git -C /src/vsim rev-parse HEAD)" = "${VSIM_REV}" \
 && cd /src/vsim \
 && RTL=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys; c=yaml.safe_load(open('config.yaml'))['cpus']; \
print(c['${ENGINE}']['rtl_package'])") \
 && echo "engine ${ENGINE} needs RTL package: ${RTL}" \
 && git submodule update --init --recursive -- \
      external/andes_clarity external/andesim_abi \
      external/cpu_config_to_march_converter external/doctest external/fmt \
      external/lief external/rapidjson external/spdlog external/systemc \
      external/systemc-cci external/systemc-components external/toml11 \
      external/yaml-cpp "external/${RTL}"; \
    rc=$?; rm -f /tmp/gitcreds; exit $rc

RUN cd /src/vsim \
 && cmake -B build -G Ninja \
      -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/andescycle \
      -DVSIM_LINK_STATIC=ON \
      -DVSIM_CPUS="${ENGINE}" \
 && cmake --build build --target "sim_${ENGINE}" \
 && cmake --install build \
 && strip "/opt/andescycle/bin/sim_${ENGINE}" \
 && rm -rf /src/vsim

# --- mountpoint: an empty directory, so /opt/riscv-toolchain exists ---------
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE} AS mountpoint
RUN mkdir -p /mountpoint

# --- andesim: the driver, the handoff plugin and the runtime library ---------
FROM env AS andesim

ARG ANDESIM_REPO
ARG ANDESIM_REF
ARG ANDESIM_REV
ARG TOOLCHAIN_ID
ARG ENGINE
# ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER: the entry point's job on a host is to put the run
# inside this image. Inside the image that job is finished, so the entry point
# must run the driver rather than start a second container -- without this,
# every command a user types answers "needs podman (or docker)".
ENV QEMU_BIN_DIR=/opt/qemu/bin \
    VSIM_BIN_DIR=/opt/andescycle/bin \
    HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain \
    VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu/bin/qemu-system-riscv64 \
    VSIM_PLUGIN=/opt/andesim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so \
    ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER=1

# The mount point, left empty. It has to arrive by COPY from a stage of its
# own: the build-time --volume has the host toolchain mounted read-only over
# this path for the whole of every RUN, so a `mkdir` here would land on the
# mounted filesystem and leave nothing in the layer. COPY is not covered by
# that mount. No toolchain ships; the empty directory only gives a forgotten
# `-v` the shape a run expects, and `andesim doctor` names the missing
# compiler outright.
COPY --from=mountpoint /mountpoint /opt/riscv-toolchain

COPY --from=qemu-build   /opt/qemu       /opt/qemu
COPY --from=engine-build /opt/andescycle /opt/andescycle

# The git history goes with the clone: the driver's build stamp is baked at
# compile time, so the finished image needs no repository metadata, and
# shipping it would hand the user the machine's development history.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    install -m600 /run/secrets/gitcreds /tmp/gitcreds \
 && GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
    GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
    GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/tmp/gitcreds" \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "${ANDESIM_REF}" --recurse-submodules \
      "${ANDESIM_REPO}" /opt/andesim \
 && test "$(git -C /opt/andesim rev-parse HEAD)" = "${ANDESIM_REV}"; \
    rc=$?; rm -f /tmp/gitcreds; exit $rc
WORKDIR /opt/andesim

# The image's own config.env. Every consumer that reads it -- the driver, the
# build scripts, the test harness -- then resolves in-image paths, with no
# trace of the machine the image was built on.
RUN printf '%s\n' \
      "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}" \
      "QEMU_BIN_DIR=${QEMU_BIN_DIR}" \
      "VSIM_BIN_DIR=${VSIM_BIN_DIR}" \
      > config.env

# build_runtime.sh compiles against the mounted toolchain; only AndeSim's own
# artifacts (libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs) are
# baked. TOOLCHAIN_ID is what puts that toolchain in this layer's cache key --
# a bind mount contributes nothing to one, so without it a rebuild with a
# different toolchain would reuse artifacts compiled against the old one.
#
# vlinux.elf is built here too. `--runtime linux` boots the app under it, and
# a run happens inside this image: without it the whole Linux runtime answers
# "vlinux.elf not built" and no user can reach it.
RUN echo "runtime built against toolchain ${TOOLCHAIN_ID}" \
 && make -C qemu_plugin \
 && ./scripts/build_driver.sh \
 && ./scripts/build_runtime.sh \
 && make -C runtime/linux \
 && test -f ./build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf \
 && ./build/andesim list engines | grep -qw "${ENGINE}" \
 && test -x ./andesim \
 && rm -rf .git

ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/andesim/andesim"]

# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
#
# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
#
# Usage:
#   make            # build both
#   make clean
#
# Output (in this directory):
#   libhybrid_handoff.so    -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotIterationLoop.so  -- hot inner-loop detector (`andesim profile`)

CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

# _POSIX_C_SOURCE states what this code actually is. Both plugins use POSIX
# APIs -- write/fsync/rename/unlink, ssize_t, PATH_MAX -- and -std=c11 alone
# defines __STRICT_ANSI__, which hides every one of them behind glibc's
# __USE_POSIX guards. It builds on hosts whose libc headers happen to leak
# them and fails on ones that do not (Ubuntu 24.04, where the container image
# is built): "'PATH_MAX' undeclared".
CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11 -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)

.PHONY: all clean

all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so

libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/handoff_site.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/reg_names.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h \
                     $(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE)/qemu-plugin.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)

# hotIterationLoop is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not
# HYBRID_INCLUDE.
libhotIterationLoop.so: hotIterationLoop.c $(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE)/qemu-plugin.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotIterationLoop.c $(LIBS)

	rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so

#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andesim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

# --version's build-time half: the release tag plus the git identity of this
# checkout and of the shared ABI submodule, stamped into the binary. Re-run on
# EVERY build, not just at configure time -- a stale stamp would let the binary
# claim a commit it was not built from, the very source/binary mix-up the report
# exists to expose. The header is rewritten only when the values change, so an
# unchanged checkout costs nothing.

# Stamp the driver's build-time identity into a generated header.
#
# `andesim --version` reports four components. Two of them -- this driver and
# the shared ABI headers it is compiled against -- are built together, so their
# git identity is known at the moment the binary is produced and is baked in
# here. (The other two, QEMU and the engine, arrive as prebuilt binaries and are
# asked at run time; see driver/cmd_version.cpp.)
#
# Run via `cmake -P` from a custom target on EVERY build, not at configure time:
# a stamp that only refreshes when CMake re-runs would let the binary claim a
# commit it was not built from -- exactly the source/binary mix-up this report
# exists to expose. The header is rewritten only when its content changes, so an
# unchanged checkout never forces a recompile.
#
# Inputs (-D): REPO_ROOT  the andesim checkout
#              ABI_ROOT   the shared ABI headers (a pinned submodule)
#              VERSION_FILE  file holding the release tag, e.g. "v0.1.0"
#              OUT        the header to write
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)

find_package(Git QUIET)

# The branch the SUPERPROJECT declares for the pinned submodule checked out at
# `dir`, read from its committed .gitmodules; "" when `super` pins nothing there
# or declares no branch for it.
#
# This is what makes the ABI identity reproducible. `git submodule update
# --init` always leaves a submodule on a DETACHED HEAD, so the working tree
# alone cannot say which branch it tracks -- a fresh clone and a dev box that
# happens to have a branch checked out inside the submodule would otherwise
# report different strings for the same build. The .gitmodules declaration is
# committed in the superproject, so it travels with every clone and is the same
# for every checkout of a given superproject commit.
#
# Nothing here knows the submodule's name, path, or branch: the entry is found
# by matching `dir` against the declared paths.
function(declared_submodule_branch super dir out_var)
  set(${out_var} "" PARENT_SCOPE)
  set(modules "${super}/.gitmodules")
  if(NOT GIT_FOUND OR NOT EXISTS "${modules}")
    return()
  endif()

  get_filename_component(super_abs "${super}" ABSOLUTE)  # also normalises ".."
  get_filename_component(dir_abs "${dir}" ABSOLUTE)
  file(RELATIVE_PATH rel "${super_abs}" "${dir_abs}")

  # One "submodule.<name>.path <path>" line per registered submodule.
  execute_process(COMMAND ${GIT_EXECUTABLE} config -f ${modules}
                          --get-regexp "^submodule\\..*\\.path$"

研究完了。我看了 `andesim` 的 `Containerfile`、`scripts/`、`driver/CMakeLists.txt`、`runtime/Makefile`、`qemu_plugin/Makefile`。

## 結論: 可以，而且 BSV 幾乎剛好符合 — 但有一個真的阻礙

AndeSim 的 `Containerfile` 做的事，BSV 已經有 80%:

| Containerfile 的 stage | BSV 已經有 |
|---|---|
| `qemu-build` (clone + build QEMU) | `andes.qemu` |
| `engine-build` (clone + build vsim, `sim_<ENGINE>`) | `andes.vsim` |
| `env` (apt install cmake/ninja/clang/boost/glib/verilator…) | `build.stdenv` + `build.cmake` + `build.verilator` … |
| RISC-V toolchain (bind-mount `/opt/riscv-toolchain`) | `build.andes.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d` |
| `andesim` (driver + plugin + runtime) | ← **這是你要新增的** |

---

## 阻礙: AndeSim 用的是**不同的 repo**

`scripts/build_image.sh:37-41` vs `pkgs/andes/repositories.nix`:

| | AndeSim 用 | BSV 有 |
|---|---|---|
| QEMU | `nick/hybrid_qemu` @ `andesim` | `RD-SW/qemu` @ `andes-v5-v10.2` |
| vsim | `nick/hybrid_vsim` @ `llamacpp` | `RD-SW/vsim` @ `main` |
| engine | `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` | 沒指定 `-DVSIM_CPUS` |

還有第二個問題: **BSV 的 qemu 沒開 plugin**。`pkgs/andes/qemu/default.nix:100-109` 有 `--without-default-features`，但沒有 `--enable-plugins`。你的 `libhybrid_handoff.so` 載不進去。

這兩件事要先決定。我的建議是**先做這一步**:

1. 把 `hybrid_qemu` 的 andesim 修改合併回 `RD-SW/qemu`，`hybrid_vsim` 合併回 `RD-SW/vsim`
2. 幫 `pkgs/andes/qemu/default.nix` 加 `--enable-plugins` (這是獨立的小 PR，先送)

不合併的話，就要在 `repositories.nix` 加 `andesim-qemu` / `andesim-vsim` 兩個 entry，等於 BSV 裡有兩份 QEMU。可以，但長期會痛。

---

## AndeSim 要切成 4 個 package，跨 2 個 host

這是關鍵設計。AndeSim 的產出物**不是同一台機器跑的**:

| # | Package | host | 產出 | 範本 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `andes.andesim` | `x86_64-linux-gnu` | `andesim` 執行檔 (C++20 CMake) | `pkgs/andes/vsim` |
| 2 | `andes.andesim-plugin` | `x86_64-linux-gnu` | `libhybrid_handoff.so`、`libhotIterationLoop.so` (`make`, 需要 glib) | `pkgs/andes/libdsp` |
| 3 | `nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d.andesim-runtime` | **RISC-V** | `libandesim_runtime.a`, `crt0.o`, `andesim.ld`, `andesim.specs`, `ROI.h` | **`pkgs/andes/libnn`** |
| 4 | `nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d.andesim-vlinux` | **RISC-V** | `vlinux.elf` | 同上，依賴 #3 |

`runtime/Makefile` 用 `$(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc`，`-march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d` — 正好對上 `nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d`。`libnn` 的寫法可以照抄:

```nix
root = [ build.stdenv-nocc  build.andes.${host.name} ];
builder = lib.bashBuilder ''
  cp --archive $src/. .
  chmod --recursive u+w .
  make -C runtime TOOLCHAIN=${build.andes.${host.name}}/${build.prefix} OUT=$out/${host.prefix}
'';
```

---

## 兩個要注意的細節

**1. `fetchGit` 不含 `.git` 目錄** (`lib/fetch-git.nix` 的註解寫明)。你的 `driver/cmake/build_stamp.cmake` 會跑 `git`，在 sandbox 裡會變成 `"unknown"`。解法照 `libnn` 的做法，用 env var 傳:

```nix
env.ANDESIM_GIT_REV = src.rev;
```
(需要在 `build_stamp.cmake` 加一個 `-D` 或環境變數 override，這是 andesim 那邊要小改的地方)

**2. `config.env` 要換成 wrapper script。** 現在 driver 讀 `QEMU_BIN_DIR` / `VSIM_BIN_DIR` / `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`。在 BSV 裡這些應該是 store 路徑，寫死在一個 wrapper 裡 — 就是 `pkgs/linux-gnu.nix:909` 那個 `runners` 的模式:

```nix
QEMU_BIN_DIR=${host.andes.qemu}/${host.prefix}/bin
VSIM_BIN_DIR=${host.andes.vsim}/${host.prefix}/bin
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=${host.andes.nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d}/${host.prefix}
```

這樣 `andesim doctor` 永遠找得到東西，使用者不用編輯任何 config。

---

## 我建議的順序

| 步 | 做什麼 | 為什麼先做 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pkgs/andes/qemu`: 加 `--enable-plugins` | 獨立小改動，先驗證 plugin 能載入 |
| 2 | 決定 fork 要不要合併回 RD-SW | 這決定後面所有寫法 |
| 3 | 做 #3 `andesim-runtime` | 最小、最獨立，`libnn` 可照抄，馬上有成果 |
| 4 | 做 #1 + #2 driver 和 plugin | CMake，`vsim` 可照抄 |
| 5 | 做 wrapper + `tests/andesim/` | 把 qemu/vsim/toolchain 綁起來，跑 e2e |

第 2 步是你的決定，我沒辦法幫你決。你想合併 fork，還是先在 `repositories.nix` 放兩個 andesim 專用 entry？

決定了我們就從第 3 步開始 — 那個檔案最短，你可以真正看懂每一行。
